(An example can be found here: #42041)
Mathlib CI can automatically push commits that fixes trivial whitespace problems, but this seems to cause race condition with other CI and indefinitely cancel them, resulting in a PR in a CI-failed state until the next push. Maybe some timing should be tweaked in the auto-commit CI?
I've manually retriggered CI on that PR and I'll take a look to see if there's something we can do tomorrow.

I've been looking into this this week and there is indeed a race condition where the pre-commit job can pre-empt the actual build job and they both end up getting canceled. I'm going to propose some changes to how we're using pre-commit as well as the style lint suggest job in #mathlib4 > Is pre commit CI enabled? after I've finished up some PRs.
this can also happen without pre commit CI, if you just push twice really close in time
#43955 replaces GitHub's concurrency handling (which was prone to the race condition) with a step that checks whether the SHA is the head, which should be much more reliable.
